# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Net long positions in gold were scaled back right across Comex in the week to April 24th. Reductions in large speculative futures positions led the way as usual, accounting for more than 75% of the overall reduction. Speculators on Tocom were a little more bullish, adding 40,000 ounces worth of long positioning. Overall we have seen around 9.5m ounces of long liquidation since positioning peaked for the year at 28.5m ounces at the end of February. In the same period, the spot price has dropped by almost $150. • The heavy ETF selling in silver we have witnessed since the beginning of April slowed last week, with net outflows of 285,000 ounces (compared with more than 1 million and 2 million ounces during the previous two weeks). The largest fund kept holdings steady after a period of incessant selling. Two European funds between them accounted for all of last week’s liquidation. • Net long speculative positioning in palladium saw its biggest intraweek increase since early March as investors added a chunky 100,000 ounces. This marks a significant break with the trend, after the previous four weeks had seen positions cut back by more than 672,000 ounces. This shift accords with the generally favourable stance towards palladium that has been building in the spec market following its recent strong price performance. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **30 April 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **30 April 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 24 April 2012; ETF data to 27 April 2012.** **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

The market’s sights during the early part of the week were firmly trained on Wednesday, when Comex option expiry would shortly be followed by a Federal Open Market Committee announcement. Sure enough, the few hours around the FOMC statements were highly volatile. Gold was sold down $15 in no time to revisit Monday’s lows before sweeping right back up and closing just a few dollars higher on the day. The fact that gold made it through to the other side of Wednesday’s event risk virtually unscathed seemed to inspire some confidence in the market in the latter part of the week. Prices climbed another $20 from Thursday to Friday, with the bulk of the gains on each day coming around the US opening. Attention began to shift back towards the Eurozone by the end of the week with S&P’s downgrade of Spain’s credit rating on Thursday. A well-received auction of Italian 10-year bonds on Friday morning however helped to keep risk appetite robust into the weekend, and gold benefitted from the stronger Euro, which ended the week on a high. - Net long positions in gold were scaled back right across Comex in the week to April 24th. Reductions in large speculative futures positions led the way as usual, accounting for more than 75% of the overall reduction. Speculators on Tocom were a little more bullish, adding 40,000 ounces worth of long positioning. Overall we have seen around 9.5m ounces of long liquidation since positioning peaked for the year at 28.5m ounces at the end of February. In the same period, the spot price has dropped by almost $150. - Gold ETFs cut their holdings for a third consecutive week, with the largest—SPDR—shedding 58,000 ounces. - Silver remains a jittery and featureless market at present. Within the firm downtrend that has established itself since the beginning of April, we have seen vicious intraday moves of $1 or more occurring on little or no fundamental newsflow and last week was no exception. The price fell almost vertically on Monday, giving up more than $1 before settling just above $30.60—the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement of the large move from December’s low to February’s high. Silver was caught up in the FOMC volatility on Wednesday, dipping briefly below $30 (for the first time since mid-January) before recovering back above the key $30.60 level. Like gold, silver continued to recover through Thursday and Friday, closing just above April’s resistance trendline. - Speculative interest in silver continues to weaken as net long positioning on Comex declined for the seventh week of the last eight. At 125 million ounces, net longs are now at their lowest level since mid-January this year. As we have noted for the last few weeks, the industrial demand picture is unclear, bordering on bearish. Each negative headline concerning the sol

ar industry (and these have been in fairly consistent supply of late) seems to damp investor bullishness before it can gather any real momentum. The most likely catalyst for a rejuvenation of spec buying in silver in the near term would be a rally in the gold price. - The heavy ETF selling in silver we have witnessed since the beginning of April slowed last week, with net outflows of 285,000 ounces (compared with more than 1 million and 2 million ounces during the previous two weeks). The largest fund kept holdings steady after a period of incessant selling. Two European funds between them accounted for all of last week’s liquidation. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **30 April 2012** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 24 April 2012; ETF data to 27 April 2012.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

After touching a low of $1,542.50 amidst the post-FOMC melee on Wednesday, the price regained $30 by Friday’s close to end the week above $1,575, down just $7 from Monday’s open. Although the bear run seen in platinum since the end of February remains intact, the pace of decline is slowing and the move may finally be beginning to bottom out. - Despite the fact that the decline seems to be slowing, speculative positioning indicates that investors remain bearish platinum for the time being. Net long specs contracted for the third consecutive week, and have now shrunk by more than 470,000 ounces since the beginning of April. There was a small increase in net long small futures positioning and in Tocom positions. - There were no flows of note in platinum ETFs last week.
